transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-08
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Leah Gomez (Redwood SE), Maya Reynolds (Carmine - Head of Platform), Tom Nguyen (Carmine - Security Engineer), Priya Kapoor (Carmine - Legal Ops)

Summary:
Quick security posture intake to evaluate whether Redwood Hosted or Dedicated (or Private) satisfies Carmine's authorization, encryption, and audit requirements. Main gating items: KMS key control, RBAC and least privilege, SSO/SAML integration with Okta, audit log retention and export, and whether Redwood can meet restrictions around customer-managed keys and data residency.

Topics:
- SOC 2 / ISO artifacts and timelines
- SSO/SAML and provisioning flows (Okta)
- RBAC and token scoping for route-level permissions
- Audit logs: granularity, retention, export to SIEM
- Encryption and KMS (bring-your-own-key) and HSM integration
- Data retention and deletion certifications

Transcript:
[00:00] Samir (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for taking time. Quick intros then we can go into the security checklist.
[00:18] Maya (Carmine): Hi, Maya here. I'm leading this evaluation alongside Tom and Priya. We're mostly trying to see gating controls for a pilot across customer data.
[00:26] Tom (Carmine): Tom, security engineer. Focus on key control, audit logs, and the SSO integration flow.
[00:33] Priya (Carmine): Priya from legal, short window — we need to understand data retention egress and contract language for logs.
[00:40] Leah (Redwood SE): Great. Quick note on roles: Samir will handle commercial and artifacts, I'll go technical on KMS, RBAC, and deployment patterns.
[00:49] Samir: First question: are you leaning Hosted, Dedicated, or Private for the pilot? Any hard constraints?
[00:57] Maya: Ideally Hosted for speed, but we have strict controls — we need customer-managed keys and the ability to restrict access to logs. If Hosted can't do BYOK we may have to go Dedicated.
[01:10] Tom: Also need ability to push logs to our SIEM (we use Splunk), and retention to 7 years for certain audit trails.
[01:18] Leah: Understood. Quick correction: we usually call it KV cache for the runtime; sometimes transcription shows KV cash in our docs — ha.
[01:25] Samir: (laughs) noted. On SOC artifacts: we can share our SOC 2 Type II report; we also have ISO 27001 in progress.
[01:34] Priya: When you say "share" — is that gated by an NDA or can it be posted? We usually need the SOC under an NDA for vendors.
[01:42] Samir: Yes, we can provide SOC under NDAs. We'll send the latest Type II and a summary bridge letter.
[01:49] Maya: Great. On SSO — we run Okta for provisioning, SCIM for group sync, and SAML for SSO. Need to confirm SAML integration and user mapping to RBAC roles.
[01:58] Leah: Our Console supports SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning. For Hosted, we support SAML via redirect flows and SCIM group sync. For Dedicated/Private there are additional options for custom IdP endpoints.
[02:10] Tom: How granular is RBAC? We need route-level controls so only certain teams can call specific models/routes especially when those routes touch PII.
[02:19] Leah: We support RBAC at multiple levels — org, team, route. You can restrict model access per token and tie that to Okta groups. In Dedicated we can also do network-level restrictions so inference plane is isolated.
[02:30] Maya: Can RBAC be enforced on streaming responses and function calling? We do a lot of tool-calls in our flows.
[02:36] Leah: Yes, permissions control which integrations can be used per route. I will follow up with a diagram of route->permission mapping.
[02:44] Tom: Encryption: BYOK is a hard requirement for production. Does Hosted allow customer-managed KMS keys or is that only for Dedicated/Private?
[02:55] Samir: Hosted supports envelope encryption with customer keys for some enterprise tiers — we integrate with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and customer-HSM via an integration. For strict BYOK you may prefer Dedicated or Private where keys never leave your VPC.
[03:10] Tom: Ok, can you clarify the key rotation and access logs on the KMS side? We need to see who used the key and when.
[03:18] Leah: Key usage is logged in KMS audit trails — we also surface access events in our audit logs. For Hosted, key usage is proxied; we provide logs with correlation IDs that you can map back to KMS logs. We'll include a sample correlation file.
[03:32] Priya: About audit logs — we need immutability guarantees and export to our Splunk instance. Retention requirements sometimes exceed default retention windows.
[03:42] Leah: You can push audit streams to a customer-managed S3 or to your SIEM via secure delivery. Retention policies are configurable per tenant; default is 90 days in Console, but enterprise can request longer retention and archival.
[03:57] Maya: 7 years is non-negotiable for some datasets. Is long-term archival supported? Will that be an extra charge?
[04:05] Samir: Long-term archival is supported for logs and can be exported to your S3. There is an additional storage fee; we'll flag that in the pilot estimate.
[04:14] Tom: About access: can we enforce MFA on service tokens or restrict IP ranges for API calls?
[04:22] Leah: For human users, SSO + MFA is standard. For service tokens, you can bind tokens to IP allowlists and to short-lived credentials issued via an internal broker. In Dedicated/Private you can also lock down to VPC endpoints.
[04:35] Maya: For legal risk, we need deletion certs when data is deleted — can Redwood provide proof of deletion for vectors/cache entries?
[04:44] Samir: We provide deletion receipts for persisted data in storage tiers. For runtime artifacts like KV cache, we have TTL controls and can provide a deletion audit showing when keys and caches were evicted. We'll clarify scope — sometimes ephemeral runtime data is not archived.
[04:58] Tom: The vector DB question — do you persist embeddings? We want to ensure that embeddings derived from PII are treated as PII and subject to deletion.
[05:06] Leah: Embeddings may be cached for performance; customers can opt out of persistent embedding storage or configure immediate deletion post-inference. For Hosted, default caching for latency improvements exists but is configurable per route.
[05:18] Maya: On data residency — we need EU-only residency for a subset of data. How do you handle regional routing?
[05:27] Leah: We support regional routing by policy. Hosted routes requests to regional clusters based on customer config and can pin model variants to regions. For strict EU-only contracts, Dedicated or Private in EU region is recommended.
[05:39] Priya: Any SOC or ISO certification timelines? We need evidence of current coverage.
[05:45] Samir: SOC 2 Type II report available now; ISO 27001 is planned and we can share the roadmap.
[05:52] Tom: How about pen test results and vulnerability scans?
[05:56] Leah: We do quarterly pen tests and weekly vuln scans; we can provide a redacted executive summary and remediation timelines.
[06:06] Maya: For our procurement, we also need to know about subprocessor list and third-party hosting details.
[06:12] Samir: We'll attach the current subprocessor list and a hosting topology diagram showing third-party SaaS and cloud providers.
[06:20] Tom: Any limitations on legal hold for customer logs? We need to place holds on specific records in support of investigations.
[06:29] Leah: We support legal hold workflows on exported logs; inside the platform you can flag retention rules per dataset. For Hosted, holds are applied at export/archival layers. For Dedicated/Private you get more direct control.
[06:42] Maya: For encryption, can you do HSM-backed keys with FIPS 140-2 validation?
[06:49] Leah: Yes, we support HSM-backed keys and can integrate with FIPS-compliant KMS providers. We'll include a short note on supported KMS/HSM vendors.
[06:59] Tom: We also have to make sure API-level token scoping supports least privilege — e.g., tokens that can only create embeddings and not call the chat endpoints.
[07:09] Leah: That's possible. Tokens can be scoped to routes, methods, and models. We'll show an example token policy.
[07:16] Maya: Regarding the audit trail format — do you use a common schema (e.g., ECS) to make ingestion straightforward?
[07:22] Leah: We can export in JSON structured logs; we map events to common fields and can align to ECS or a custom schema for your SIEM.
[07:31] Samir: Quick check — any blockers from your side that would push you to Private instead of Hosted?
[07:38] Tom: BYOK plus our 7-year log retention and EU-only residency for certain workloads. If Hosted can fully meet those with contractual SSAs, fine; otherwise Dedicated.
[07:50] Priya: Also need data processing addendum tweaks and indemnities for certain regulatory classes.
[07:57] Samir: We can engage legal to look at DPA and liability buckets. We'll provide standard language and mark up potential changes.
[08:06] Maya: Do you support SOC2 + PCI scope limitations? Some of our customers handle payments.
[08:11] Leah: We're not PCI-certified, but you can isolate PCI workloads in a Private deployment; we can help design a scope-limited deployment so Redwood isn't in the PCI scope for your systems.
[08:24] Tom: For logging fidelity, can we get raw request/response bodies (redacted)? Or at least metadata and correlation IDs so we can reconstruct flows?
[08:33] Leah: We do not provide raw customer content in regular audit exports for privacy reasons, but metadata, token IDs, and correlation IDs are available; with a legal request we can provide more in a controlled manner.
[08:48] Maya: How do you handle alerts for suspicious activity — e.g., tokens being used anomalously?
[08:54] Leah: We have built-in anomaly detection for rate spikes and unusual model usage and you can forward alerts to your Ops channel. In Dedicated we can also integrate with your SIEM for custom rules.
[09:05] Priya: On the legal side, retention obligations — do you provide automated deletion reports and attestations?
[09:12] Samir: We provide deletion receipts and can run attestations for data destruction. We'll add an attestation template in the follow-up materials.
[09:21] Tom: About ingress/egress encryption — TLS is default, but do you support mTLS for connectors between your control plane and our VPC?
[09:30] Leah: Yes — mTLS is supported for private peering and control plane connections in Dedicated/Private setups. For Hosted, we rely on TLS+authn for control plane interactions but can discuss custom peering.
[09:45] Maya: If we do a pilot on Hosted with BYOK, latency is a concern. How does BYOK affect request latency?
[09:53] Leah: There's a small overhead for envelope encryption KMS lookups on first use; we mitigate with local envelope caching and async key ops. For tight SLAs, Dedicated with colocated KMS reduces that overhead.
[10:07] Samir: Let's talk about timelines — what's your procurement window?
[10:11] Maya: Targeting a pilot by mid-November, procurement signoff by end of November if the security gating is ok.
[10:18] Samir: Great. We'll prioritize SOC docs and the pilot runbook.
[10:24] Tom: A couple fine-grain questions — route-level logging, can we include the prompt hash instead of full prompt for privacy?
[10:33] Leah: You can opt for hashed prompt references in logs; we support storing prompt hashes rather than content in export streams.
[10:40] Maya: About dataset deletion requests from EU users — do you provide GDPR subject access / erasure workflows?
[10:47] Leah: Yes. We provide support for DSARs and have documented workflows. For Hosted, we run erasure through our control plane and generate deletion receipts; for Dedicated we can hand over the tooling.
[10:58] Priya: Will you require us to sign any additional SSO or SCIM contracts or is that covered in standard terms?
[11:05] Samir: Standard terms cover SSO/SCIM integrations; if you need additional SLAs or uptime for the SCIM sync we'll include that in Dedicated contracts.
[11:16] Tom: Are there rate limits on audit log exports? If we push high-volume logs to S3 or SIEM, do you throttle?
[11:25] Leah: Exports to customer S3 are batched; SIEM export pipelines have throughput considerations — we'll include recommended batching configs to avoid throttling.
[11:36] Maya: Any limitations on service accounts and number of SCIM groups? We have a large org structure.
[11:42] Leah: SCIM scales, but for very large directories we recommend a Dedicated plan and a scoping session to tune sync windows.
[11:52] Samir: Ok, quick recap and ownership for next steps.
[11:55] (fast-forward) Remaining portion: Samir recaps artifacts, Leah to produce pilot runbook, Tom to return questionnaire.

Recap / Next steps:
- Samir to send SOC2 Type II, subprocessor list, and redacted pen-test exec summary (by 2026-10-12).
- Leah to draft pilot runbook detailing Hosted vs Dedicated configuration, KMS options, RBAC examples, and log export sample schema (by 2026-10-15).
- Tom to circulate vendor questionnaire internally and return to Samir (by 2026-10-20).
- Legal: Priya to review DPA and flag any non-standard clauses (align with Samir week of 2026-10-12).

[12:08] Samir: we'll get those docs over, thanks.
